beats.text: Four centuries of empire. Gone in one summer.
1895. Cuba rose up against Spain once again. Just across the water, Americans watched closely.
beats.say: Eighteen ninety-five. Cuba rose up against Spain once again. Just across the water, Americans watched closely.

beats.text: Then the American battleship Maine blew up in Havana harbour. Two hundred and sixty-six men died.
American newspapers blamed Spain. Remember the Maine! Later studies suggest it may have been a fire inside the ship.
War came in April. At Manila, an American squadron wiped out Spain's Pacific fleet within hours.
In July, Spain's Atlantic fleet tried to break out of Santiago. Every ship was lost.
By December it was over. Spain gave up Cuba, and handed Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines to the United States.
A year later, Spain sold its last Pacific islands to Germany.
It had begun in 1492, with three small ships. Four centuries later, it was gone.
beats.say: It had begun in fourteen ninety-two, with three small ships. Four centuries later, it was gone.

beats.text: Spaniards simply called it the Disaster. A generation of writers asked: what is Spain now?
